spec_match.rationale: The three break modes (missing ACAO, new preflight, Local Network Access) are the real consequences of routing Background Fetch through the fetch pipeline, and the URL classifier applies the same origin/loopback/private-range rules the pipeline does.

interactive.rationale: A textarea-driven audit tool classifies each pasted URL into unaffected/check/risk rows with a tally, pre-populated and auto-run on load; verified the default six URLs produce 1 same / 2 check / 3 risk.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The feature-index card says the three failure modes are 'checked against what this browser actually reports', but the page is a purely static classifier plus reference table — nothing on it queries the browser or the service worker.

edge_cases.rationale: The classifier handles unparseable strings, protocol-relative URLs, loopback spellings, link-local and all RFC1918 private ranges, each with a distinct verdict.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6210300985606144, the Fetch CORS protocol, and cross-links the sibling Local Network Access feature.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves the underlying opaque-vs-cors contract, but its background-fetch-requires-user-activation assertion reads FAIL rather than blocked on a fresh profile with no service worker registration — flagged for a human, not edited.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): page auto-ran the audit (console: audited 6 {same:1,check:2,risk:3}), rows and tally rendered correctly, console clean, no failed same-origin requests; desktop 1280 and mobile 360 screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: Loads demo-telemetry.js and emits a urls-audited assert with the tally on every run.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, same/check/risk colours from accent variables, button colour pair overridden together, interactive tool rather than a static card.

accessibility.rationale: The textarea has a real label, both tables have captions and scoped row/column headers, the tally is an aria-live output, and verdicts are conveyed as text not colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: No horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 (scrollWidth 360, screenshot read); the four-column audit table is cramped but wraps legibly without clipping.

openQuestions.title: Deliver the browser check the blurb promises, or soften the blurb
openQuestions.detail: The feature-index card ends 'checked against what this browser actually reports', but the audit is entirely static URL classification. Either add a live verification step — e.g. for a reachable URL, run a HEAD/no-cors fetch to report whether Access-Control-Allow-Origin is actually present, or run a one-record background fetch against the showcase's own cross-origin pair to show the worker-side symptom for the visitor's build — or reword the card so it does not claim a browser-backed check the page does not perform.

summary: Reviewed at http://localhost:3000/v154/cors-enforcement-for-background-fetch/what-changed/ with Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp). The audit tool auto-ran its six default URLs and classified them correctly (1 unaffected, 2 CORS-check, 3 CORS+LNA risk), the three-break-modes table matches the real enforcement consequences, console/network were clean bar the sandbox font-CDN artifact, and desktop 1280 plus mobile 360 DPR3 screenshots showed no overflow. The one real gap is honesty of framing: the card's 'checked against what this browser actually reports' oversells a purely static classifier. Feature /conformance/ ran 6 pass / 1 fail, the fail being the fresh-profile user-activation assertion flagged for human review.
